terms.meaning: A set of tasks the user has ticked, so one action can be applied to all of them.
A small colored label showing how urgent a task is.
A shared place in the app where task data is kept and changed.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Brings in React, the task and status types, the shared store, the badge component and the play, edit and delete icons. Marks the file as running in the browser.
sections.why: Likely reason: the table needs the store for its actions and browser events for clicks.
sections.watch_out: The Edit icon is imported but does not appear in the shown code, so it may be a leftover from an earlier edit button.

sections.name: TaskTableProps
sections.title: Inputs for the table
sections.what: Says what the parent must provide: the tasks to show, the ids of selected tasks, and a function to toggle one task's selection.
sections.why: Likely reason: the parent keeps selection so the bulk actions bar can read the same list.
sections.watch_out: The table trusts the parent's selected list, so an id left over from a previous filter still shows as selected.

sections.name: TaskTable (part 1)
sections.title: Table headings and main columns
sections.what: Draws the column headings, a checkbox for each row, the title with a line through it when completed, a status dropdown, and a priority badge.
sections.why: Likely reason: the status dropdown sits in the row so a user can change status while scanning many tasks.
sections.watch_out: Medium and low priorities both use a plain indigo badge here, so this table looks different from the card view, which uses other colors.

sections.name: TaskTable (part 2)
sections.title: Category, date, time and row buttons
sections.what: Shows the category, or General if none is set, the due date, or No date if none is set, and the estimate in minutes. Adds a focus timer button and a delete button to each row. When there are no tasks, shows one message across the table.
sections.why: Likely reason: plain fallback text keeps empty fields from looking broken.
sections.watch_out: Delete removes the task at once with no confirmation, and there is no edit button in this table.

summary: Shows many tasks in a compact table with a checkbox per row, a status dropdown, a focus timer button and a delete button.
purpose: Let the user scan and act on many tasks at once.
why: Likely reason: a table fits many tasks on screen and makes status changes quick without opening each task.
how: 1. Receives the task list and the list of selected task ids from its parent. 2. Draws table headings. 3. For each task, draws a checkbox, the title, a status dropdown, a priority badge, category, due date, estimate, focus timer and delete buttons. 4. Shows a single message across the table when the list is empty.
inputs: A list of tasks, a list of selected task ids, and a function that toggles a selection.
outputs: A table on screen. Status changes, deletes and focus timer starts go through the shared store.
risks: Delete happens at once with no confirmation. The table has no edit option, so title and detail changes must be made elsewhere. The Edit icon is imported but not used.
debug: If a row action does nothing, check the matching store action and the task id. If a checkbox does not update, check the selected list passed from the parent. If empty fields look wrong, check the fallback text.
